turns.text: I need you to figure out which weekday in February we should hold our branch stock count. Take a look at the stock count instructions and the February dock movements in the branch folder, decide which date it should be, and create a calendar hold on that day titled Stock Count Lockdown.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
The count has to be a single weekday with zero dock movements — no inbound, no outbound, no collection — and must finish by February 19. Every Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday in the window has mill deliveries or the afternoon run booked. The only clear days are the Wednesdays the carrier depot is closed: February 10 and February 17. I picked February 10 because it sits early enough in the window that if anything goes wrong there is time to fix it before the deadline.

Here's what I found and what I set up.

**Stock count rules** — one-day count, dock closed to all movement, must be complete and submitted by Friday February 19.

**February dock movements** — mill deliveries roll in every Monday and Thursday, the afternoon run goes out every day except the Wednesdays the carrier depot is shut. That means Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday all have booked movements and can't be used.

The only weekdays with zero inbound, zero outbound and zero collection are **Wednesday February 10** and **Wednesday February 17** — the two carrier-closed days. I picked **February 10** because it sits early enough in the window that if anything goes wrong there's room to recover before the deadline.

**Calendar hold created** — **Stock Count Lockdown** on Wednesday February 10, 06:00–17:30 (dock-to-close).

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: February 10 is locked in. Curtis will know the dock is dark that day, and the sheet template is on the intranet under corporate reporting whenever you're ready to pull it down.
